A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Make-It-Animatable and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Sections and experiments can be matched reliably despite figure replacements, relocation, and appendix additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original skeleton-prediction results, Mixamo ablations, and qualitative rigging and animation experiments, including Tables 2–3 and supplementary comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports inference-time scaling and new failure and non-rest-pose examples in Figures S9 and S14.

M1.justification: The particle-based autoencoder, geometry-aware attention, coarse-to-fine sampling, structure-aware transformer, pose representation, and training objectives remain unchanged. New Section S2.3 explains implementation of the existing body-prior losses rather than introducing another loss.

E1.justification: The Mixamo, VRoid, ModelsResource, and in-the-wild coverage is retained. Figure S14 adds explicit failure scenarios involving self-intersecting poses, out-of-distribution shapes, and unintended mesh connections; additional successful non-rest poses extend already covered conditions.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain the same across the retained experiments, including the supplementary TARig, Neural Blend Shapes, Mixamo, and Anything World comparisons. The new timing curves use RigNet and TARig, both already included in v1's timing comparison in Table 1.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a timing evaluation across multiple input vertex counts in Section S4.1 and Figure S9. The retained experiments preserve their training splits, point-sampling budget, skeleton configuration, and accuracy metrics.

E4.justification: V3 adds input-size efficiency analysis and focused failure and non-rest-pose case studies in Figures S9 and S14. The existing quantitative component ablations and geometry-attention analyses remain, although several illustrative characters are replaced.

E5.justification: The reporting practice remains point estimates and qualitative examples. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests; its new timing curves also show point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their numerical results. New Figure S9 reports additional timings, including 0.62 seconds for the proposed method versus 1892 for RigNet and 103 for TARig at 12,000 vertices. V3 also adds failure and successful pose examples and replaces several qualitative comparison cases; these do not establish same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The low-rank dynamics formulations, attention equations, and ancestral-mask definitions remain unchanged, including supplementary Equations S1–S2. The expanded latent notation and body-prior implementation explanation introduce no new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about fast, unified animation preparation, support for meshes and Gaussian splats, and flexible character shapes, poses, and skeletons. The new experiments support or qualify those claims without redefining the stated contributions.

C2.justification: V1's concluding limitations concern adaptive sampling and extension to non-bipedal characters. V3 additionally discusses failures from challenging poses, unfamiliar shapes, and mesh defects, suggesting targeted training data or geometry refinement. It also explicitly explains why many baseline comparisons use near-rest poses.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-page link for code and demos and explains how body-prior losses use bone-pair lists and L1 penalties on positions or directions in Section S2.3. It also clarifies the selected autoencoder initialization; the reported hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and main related-work survey are retained. Section S4.1 adds a limited positioning refinement by contrasting RigNet's iterative processing and TARig's feed-forward regression with the proposed particle encoder's avoidance of mesh-connectivity processing.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V3 clarifies bone-attribute terminology, revises descriptions of replaced examples, adds supplementary subsections, moves the main-text tricky-case discussion into the appendix, and updates author/contact information.

P2.justification: V3 substantially refreshes qualitative panels across the teaser, comparisons, ablations, and supplementary examples. It adds the runtime plot and failure/pose figure, revises captions and table formatting, and removes the duplicated main-text tricky-case display while retaining an updated appendix version. These extensive figure-level changes go beyond renumbering or pagination.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency by adding explicit failure evidence where v1 mainly presented successful examples, and it strengthens support for efficiency claims with vertex-count timing curves. The body-prior implementation details and code/demo access information also help reproducibility. These focused gains improve the paper while its central method and main accuracy evidence remain unchanged.
